handbookNote: Batch-2 depth expansion of the Louisiana notary track, built after batch 1's 127 questions had already mined the core primary sources (La. R.S. Title 35 and the principal Civil Code articles on authentic acts, sale, mortgages, matrimonial agreements, successions, donations, and testaments) down to roughly one question per statutory clause. This batch does two things: (1) mines previously under-tested Title 35 provisions (parish-cluster jurisdiction, the notary database and address-change duty at R.S. 35:191.2-.3, bond recordation mechanics at R.S. 35:192, annual-report penalties and inactive/retired status at R.S. 35:202, Orleans deputies at R.S. 35:287) and adds scenario/fact-pattern and date-math questions across the existing topics (recording deadlines, RON eligibility by instrument type, disciplinary timelines, lesion beyond moiety on acts of sale under Civil Code arts. 2589-2600); and (2) opens four new Civil Code topic areas that a Louisiana notary's authentic-act practice directly touches but that batch 1 did not yet cover: matrimonial regimes and community property (arts. 2325-2376, governing the matrimonial agreements and spousal-concurrence rules notaries must apply when passing acts affecting community property), intestate succession/representation/forced-heirship mechanics (arts. 870-902, 934-936, plus scenario math on the arts. 1493/1495 legitime), donation capacity/nullity/revocation-for-ingratitude (arts. 1467-1484, 1556-1560), and contractual capacity and the absolute/relative nullity distinction (arts. 1918-1926, 2029-2035) that governs when a notary's act can be undone and by whom. All of it stays inside notarial practice -- matrimonial agreements, successions, and donations a Louisiana notary actually passes -- rather than drifting into the separately-tracked LA real estate license content (servitudes, leases, condominium ownership, redhibition) covered by the la_real_estate track.
